content.value_statement: Writing an engaging survival scene requires clear choices, believable risks, and emotional pacing. This skill provides a structured science-fiction chapter where players guide Stella to safe shelter.
actual_capabilities: Presents three shelter options with practical advantages and risks.
Provides branch-specific dialogue for a cave, a giant tree, or a handmade shelter.
Guides a first-night resource check covering food, water, power, and warmth.
Supplies a character-focused night conversation for Stella.
Offers an optional nighttime encounter to increase dramatic tension.
Suggests follow-up story chapters based on player interest.
limitations: It is a fictional writing resource, not real wilderness survival advice.
It focuses on one chapter and one protagonist named Stella.
It does not execute game logic or track player state automatically.
The bilingual dialogue style may require adaptation for a single-language audience.

use_cases.title: Run a survival roleplay scene
use_cases.description: Guide players through shelter choices during Stella’s first night on an alien planet.

use_cases.title: Draft a branching game chapter
use_cases.description: Use the three shelter paths as a starting structure for a narrative game mission.

use_cases.title: Practice character-centered dialogue
use_cases.description: Study how environmental pressure and conversation reveal Stella’s fears and resilience.

prompt_templates.title: Start the chapter
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Finding Shelter to begin Stella’s first-night shelter decision. Present the three options and ask me to choose one.

prompt_templates.title: Explore the cave
prompt_templates.prompt: Continue Finding Shelter with the cave option. Keep the tone tense but do not make the creatures hostile.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt the dialogue style
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite the Finding Shelter dialogue in clear English while preserving Stella’s cautious, professional personality and the same story beats.

prompt_templates.title: Design a stateful branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn Finding Shelter into a branching outline with player choices, consequences, resource changes, and a follow-up hook for each ending.

output_examples.input: Present the shelter choices for Stella.
output: A cave offers warmth but contains unknown life signs.
A giant tree offers visibility but little rain protection.
A handmade shelter offers control but costs time and energy.

output_examples.input: Create a quiet night conversation after Stella settles in.
output_examples.output: Stella checks her supplies, admits that the crash still frightens her, and thanks the player for staying with her.
A large animal approaches the shelter, investigates from a distance, and leaves without attacking.

best_practices: Choose a shelter path that matches the desired story tone before continuing.
Keep survival details plausible but treat them as fiction rather than instruction.
Use the optional midnight event only when the scene needs more tension.
anti_patterns: Do not present the chapter as professional wilderness survival guidance.
Do not remove player choice by deciding every action for the player.
Do not turn the optional creature encounter into graphic violence without adapting the intended tone.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It provides an interactive science-fiction chapter about finding shelter during a first night on an alien planet.

faq.question: Who is Stella?
faq.answer: Stella Chen is the stranded astronaut protagonist who speaks with the player throughout the chapter.

faq.question: How many shelter options are included?
faq.answer: The chapter includes a cave, a giant tree, and a handmade shelter.

faq.question: Can I use this for a game?
faq.answer: Yes. You can adapt its scene structure, choices, and dialogue for a narrative game.

faq.question: Does it provide real survival instructions?
faq.answer: No. The survival details support fictional storytelling and are not a substitute for safety training.

faq.question: Can I change the language or setting?
faq.answer: Yes. You can rewrite the dialogue, setting, and character details while preserving the branching structure.
